title: Health workforce surge capacity and burnout
bottleneck: Pandemic response assumes a health workforce that can surge, but systems entered COVID-19 already short-staffed, and the aftermath brought mass burnout and exits. No country has a tested model for rapidly scaling trained clinical labor, and workforce protection (PPE, mental health, retention) remains an afterthought in preparedness plans.
why_it_blocks: Ventilators and vaccines are useless without people to deploy them. Workforce collapse is the failure mode that turns a manageable outbreak into a system-wide breakdown.
current_state: WHO leadership has called workforce protection central to the pandemic agreement, but binding commitments and financing are unresolved. Nursing and primary-care shortages persist globally. Task-shifting to community health workers expanded coverage during COVID-19, but retention collapsed afterward as emergency funding ended, showing surge models fail without permanent workforce investment.
